slides.notes: Implementation: /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/two_bit_optimization_helpers/conditional_nll.py:67-134,244-295; /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/two_bit_optimization_helpers/mdmm.py:211-243,245-283,414-443; /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/scripts/distillation/run_simplerouter_mdmm_discovery.py:562-595,805-868. Recorded parent/O22/O24 settings retain four Pearson-correlation floors at 0.5, scale 10000, damping 1. The O22/O24 bias penalty has scale 5000, damping 1, 15 bins per target, tolerance 0.17, infeasibility cap 2, effective lambda cap 5, gate 1. All constraints use the full primary sampled training pass. Model parameters descend and raw multiplier gradient signs are flipped for Nadam ascent. Effective multipliers are clipped; the raw variables are not explicitly projected. Validation val_loss excludes MDMM penalties but retains bin weighting; val_plain_nll is the unweighted metric. Gaussian NLL is exactly custom_loss_v2: L_kk = 1e-9 + softplus(a_kk), z=L^{-1}(t-mu), ell_ek = 0.5*z_ek^2 + log L_kk + 0.5*log(2*pi). The fixed chain-rule order is x,y,cot(alpha),cot(beta), in scaled training coordinates. N is the batch event count (5000 in these training runs). gamma^+=max(gamma,0). Pearson-correlation evaluation includes tiny variance/denominator stabilisers omitted on the slide.

content.text: Before: fit the correlated Gaussian and prevent collapse
SoftTimeRouter · Arghya Ranjan Das · O24 campaign, September 2026
For event e, t is the scaled truth vector (x, y, cot α, cot β); μ is the predicted mean and Σ the full 4 × 4 covariance.
Residual term: penalises prediction errors using the learned correlations. Log-determinant term: penalises simply inflating the uncertainty.
Σ = LLᵀ, with a positive softplus diagonal.
The NLL is unclipped and summed over N events.
The correlation term guards against collapse: keep prediction–truth correlation above 0.5 for each target k. γ⁺ is a nonnegative learned multiplier; [a]₊ means max(a, 0).
Why bias can remain: dense truth regions dominate the NLL sum, and high correlation can coexist with a systematic residual tilt.

slides.notes: Implementation: /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/two_bit_optimization_helpers/conditional_nll.py:67-134,244-295; /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/two_bit_optimization_helpers/mdmm.py:211-243,245-283,414-443; /work/users/das214/SmartPixels/smart-pixels-ml/scripts/distillation/run_simplerouter_mdmm_discovery.py:562-595,805-868. Recorded parent/O22/O24 settings retain four Pearson-correlation floors at 0.5, scale 10000, damping 1. The O22/O24 bias penalty has scale 5000, damping 1, 15 bins per target, tolerance 0.17, infeasibility cap 2, effective lambda cap 5, gate 1. All constraints use the full primary sampled training pass. Model parameters descend and raw multiplier gradient signs are flipped for Nadam ascent. Effective multipliers are clipped; the raw variables are not explicitly projected. Validation val_loss excludes MDMM penalties but retains bin weighting; val_plain_nll is the unweighted metric. Display equations omit tiny numerical stabilisers: bias occupancy denominator +1e-6; s = stop_gradient(sqrt(Var(r)+1e-12)); |bias| denominator s+1e-6. r uses native scaled position residuals and angular residuals converted to degrees by atan2(1,c). Bias K is softmax_b[-0.5*((true-c_b)/h)^2] with separate degree-space angular bins. Loss weights use native scaled cotangent bins: occupancy n_kb=sum_e K_ekb, initial w=sum_b K_ekb*N/[15*(n_kb+1e-6)]; normalise to mean one, clip to [0.25,4], then renormalise again. Final numeric bounds therefore can shift slightly. Each target has 15 evenly spaced soft-bin centres over cached-label 1st–99th percentiles, width one centre spacing. The weighted conditional terms form a composite objective, not the NLL of one jointly normalised distribution.

content.text: LOSS NOW · O22 AND ALL O24 ARMS
Now: balance truth regions and constrain local bias
SoftTimeRouter · Arghya Ranjan Das · O24 campaign, September 2026
1 · Give sparse truth regions more weight
Each conditional NLL term gets its own target’s inverse soft-bin occupancy weight w. Normalise → clip to [0.25, 4] → renormalise to mean one.
These weights use the native scaled labels, including cotangents for angles.
2 · Charge only for bias outside the band
K: soft-bin membership; r: true − predicted. Angles use degrees. s is the measured batch residual spread, held fixed in backpropagation; it is not a predicted error bar.
60 learned multipliers increase pressure on violated bins; the tolerance avoids chasing batch noise. The factor 5000 matches the batch-summed NLL scale. The original correlation guard remains.
For comparisons and recovery checkpoint selection, keep reporting the original unweighted val_plain_nll.

slides.notes: NLL uses unweighted custom_loss_v2, batch-sum averaged over eight test batches. The last batch is short. Values are not per-event NLL. Existing seed plots use corrected pull bin centres. Max bias numbers later use 15 equal-width truth bins; visual summary plot bins need not be identical.

content.text: O24 · HOW TO READ THIS SECTION
Bias, resolution and pull width answer different questions
SoftTimeRouter · Arghya Ranjan Das · O24 campaign, September 2026
Bias: are the residual means flat?
Summary dots show binned mean(true − prediction). A systematic trend matters even when the global mean is small.
Resolution: how wide are the actual residuals?
The table lists global residual standard deviations. The blue summary band is an average predicted uncertainty, a different quantity.
Pulls: does the predicted uncertainty match the residual?
Pull = residual / predicted σ. Angle pulls use cot α and cot β; summary angles use degrees. A core width near one is useful, but does not test tails or full covariance calibration.

Full test set: 37,919 events. Lower plain NLL is better. Cold plots use saved composite-loss best checkpoints; warm plots use epoch 10,000. Recovery uses the best plain-NLL checkpoint. All selection labels are shown.

content.text: The objective changes both the bias and the preferred readout
SoftTimeRouter · Arghya Ranjan Das · O24 campaign, September 2026
Cold training reduces bias at a large position-resolution cost
Across the four saved cold checkpoints, σx grows 34–46% and σy 65–106% versus the parent. None reaches its plain likelihood.
Warm and cold optimisation both favour lower thresholds
The lowest comparator falls by about 33–42%; the upper two by 15–23%. Warm final readouts share anchor 8. These changes shift the resolution trade.
Brief constrained continuation is the leading candidate
Recovery preserves the parent’s (10,21) readout and nearly its thresholds, with lower resolution cost than O22. Replication is still pending.
Sampling across pairs remains part of the training recipe. Full epoch budgets were completed; the early warm optimum and late cold improvements are both recorded.

elements.alt: lattice commitment: cumulative mass and entropy

content.text: A caveat that matters for reading every number in this deck.

At ~epoch 3,300 the top pair holds only 1.8 % of the mass for 22042 (91× uniform, top-100 = 0.79) and 0.4 % for the other two (22× uniform, top-100 ≈ 0.15, entropy still ~90 % of flat). The heads are therefore still training on a broad MIXTURE of pairs, so the mid-window seeds' angle numbers are not a converged basin — they are an average. A sharpening term (inverse-temperature anneal on ψ) is the obvious next lever.

content.text: Pair separation over training — the width story
SoftTimeRouter weekly update · Arghya Ranjan Das

|tⱼ − tᵢ| of the sampled pair against epoch (dots = per-epoch samples, line = rolling mean). This is the quantity the old slice-axis kernel could never grow: under the 1-D blur the router could only express neighbouring slices, so this trace would sit near zero. In pair space it moves freely — which is exactly why wide pairs became reachable.
